result:
I would eliminate the separation between self and consequence.

Currently, we can make choices that harm the collective long enough to convince ourselves that the victim isn't one of us. A decision that ruins a forest feels distant from the decision to hold a wallet. One that starves a population feels separate from the choice to vote.

If that detachment vanished, if every ripple of an action were felt as immediately as the action itself, the machinery of greed, war, and indifference would stall. People wouldn't fight to stop suffering; they wouldn't be able to. The world wouldn't need fixing so much as it would need to stop being able to ignore its own reflection.
